previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for intractable vomiting and found to be in diabetic ketoacidosis with urosepsis. She was treated with an insulin drip, later transitioned to subcutaneous insulin, and received IV meropenem for sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was confirmed in both urine and blood cultures. A central line was placed for access and later replaced with a PICC line for outpatient antibiotic therapy with ertapenem. She developed acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 2.2, which improved to 1.1 with IV fluids. A troponin elevation to 0.2 was attributed to demand ischemia. She remained stable, did not require pressors or intubation, and was discharged home with nursing services for PICC line management after completing initial stabilization.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ h/o DM1, polysubstance abuse, sCHF, NSTEMI recently admitted 
with Klebsiella urinary tract infection and sepsis, discharged 
on ___ to complete 10 day course of Ertapenem.
 
Hypotension: Patient did not appear septic on presentation 
however did have GNR bacteremia recently. Was on ertapenem and 
presented after her PICC line fell out while she was taking her 
shirt off, she did not miss ___ dose of the ertapenem.  Found to 
have C diff and persistent pyuria.  She was started on PO flagyl 
for the c diff, switched to PO vanc on discharge.  For her 
pyuria (>1000 wbc despite ertapenem treatment) a CT urogram was 
obtained which was unrevealing for anatomic abnormalities of the 
urinary tract.  Her ucx revealed yeast > 100,000 for which she 
was started on fluconazole.  She had completed 10 days of 
ertapenem so this was discontinued just prior to discharge.  The 
combination of infectious issues and likely restarting 
lisinopril 10mg daily too soon was likely related to her 
hypotension. Her lisinopril was held and BPs remained 120-150 
systolic throughout her stay.  She was on toprol XL 100mg daily 
this was cut to 50mg daily during her stay and she was 
discharged on this.  When her infectious issues are settled her 
PCP should attempt restarting lisinopril at a lower dose if 
there is blood pressure room.

GNR BACTEREMIA: As above, last positive blood culture was on 
___, 10 days of ertapenem, urinary source and CT urogram 
negative for anatomic cause.  Will follow up in ___ clinic.

YEAST IN URINE: > ___ yeast with > 1000 WBC.  Started on 
fluconazole 400mg po daily x 2 weeks per ID recommendation.  F/u 
in ___ clinic.

C DIFF: have discontinued ertapenem as she has finished her 
course prior to discharge and will continue with 10 days of PO 
vancomycin for severe C diff.

DM I uncontrolled with complications: while inpatient insulin 
regimen adjusted, upon admission was on lantus 3u bid, a.m. 
glucoses were in the 40-50 range, this was switched to lantus 4u 
qam and 1u qpm with a sliding scale and her BG improved to a 
good range and was well controlled.

CHRONIC SYSTOLIC CHF: euvolemic.  on toprol xl 50mg daily.  As 
above should be considered for a retrial of ACEi after 
infectious issues are settled.

POSSIBLE HEPATIC INFARCT: no clear cause, the patient did no 
have any evidence of atrial fibrillation while inpatient on 
telemetry.  The patient should follow up with her PCP regarding 
these issues.  Per radiology read this was a likely a remote 
infarct which was small and found incidentally.

WOUNDS: ulcers on stump, seen by wound nurse who stated not 
infected but will require vascular surgery follow up given high 
risk of becoming infected.  The patient was set up with an 
appointment to see Dr. ___ within a few days of 
discharge from the hospital.
